outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: The formatting/labeling of the agent’s response (numbered list, extra parentheticals like “on the #metadata view”) is not important.

Critical issues: (1) Several reported fields are not supported by what the agent actually surfaced in the Europeana UI shown in the screenshots: the title “The Milkmaid,” the providing institution “Rijksmuseum,” and the type “Art of painting” are not visible anywhere in the captured record view. Given the task’s requirement to report fields “exactly as displayed,” asserting values that were not shown constitutes likely fabrication/unsupported reporting. (2) The “type of item” is particularly problematic: “Art of painting” does not match the kind of canonical Europeana item type label typically shown (e.g., IMAGE), and no such label is visible; the only visible related info is technical “Format image/jpeg,” which the agent did not use.

What is supported: The agent did open the correct Europeana URL per action history (so the correct record constraint is likely satisfied). The screenshots clearly show “Creation date: 2013” in the Media metadata panel and “Rights: Public Domain,” matching the agent’s creation date and rights statement. The identifier 90402/SK_A_2344 is supported by the starting URL/action history even though it is not visible in-page.

Outcome: Because the user’s deliverable is all six fields taken exactly from the record display, and three of the six fields (title, providing institution, type) are not evidenced and at least one (“type”) appears plausibly wrong/invented, the agent did not successfully complete the task from an average user’s perspective. The user cannot trust the reported metadata as faithfully extracted from the record.
outcome.primary_intent: Extract and report six specific metadata fields (title, creation date, providing institution, item type, rights statement, and identifier) exactly as displayed on the Europeana record 90402/SK_A_2344 for “The Milkmaid,” without substituting another record or following external institution links. A reasonable user would not be flexible on wrong/made-up field values or missing fields, and especially not flexible on “exactly as displayed” requirements for creation date, rights wording, and identifier.
